title: My life is an open book, wish ill for no one: Shivakumar
excerpt: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Wednesday said he does not wish ill upon anyone, including former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, asserting that his life is an open book and that he has always worked with the intention of doing good for others. Speaking at the release of researcher Ramya's book, "Chalisuva Bande D. K. Shivakumar", a research-based biographical book documenting his life and political journey, at the Senate Hall in Manasagangothri here, Shivakumar said he would use his tenure in office to carry out work that would remain in the hearts of the people."I have worked with Siddaramaiah. I do not wish ill upon him or anyone else. I have never been a person who wishes harm to others and will not do so in the future either. This is my commitment," he said. Shivakumar said his life was an open book and that there were no secrets in it. "Anyone can know about my life. We love and respect people of all castes and religions. Humanity is more important than anything else," he said. The Chief Minister said navigating politics was not easy and that some people were waiting to see what he would do if given a few months to govern. He said the opposition was unable to accept his growth but added that he would not bow down to criticism."I have faith not only in myself but also in the people of this state. I have no intention of cheating, troubling or wishing harm to anyone," he said. Recalling his political differences with Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy, Shivakumar said that when the Congress decided to join hands with him, he never intended to cause Kumaraswamy any trouble and instead tried to strengthen his hands."Whether he accepts us or not is not important. It is enough if our conscience accepts what we do. There is nothing greater than one's conscience," he said. Shivakumar said receiving his degree through the University of Mysore's Open University at around the age of 48 was one of the happiest moments of his life."The happiness I experienced on receiving my degree was greater than the joy of becoming a Cabinet Minister or Chief Minister. It was a historic day in my life," he said. He recalled receiving an election ticket while studying in the final year of his degree and said that although he lost the election, he continued his political journey. The Chief Minister also spoke about the importance of books, saying they not only imparted knowledge but also provided a perspective on life."Some believe they can win through weapons. But people can be won through hearts and words. Buildings may become old, and wealth may pass into other hands, but the knowledge we gain from books can be shared with the world," he said. Shivakumar said he believed in creating history rather than merely reading it and credited four decades of hard work, political experience and the support of people and party workers for his rise to the present position. Recalling his time in jail, Shivakumar said he never lost his self-confidence even during the difficult phase."Even when I went to jail, I did not lose my confidence. I had faith that I would come out, rebuild the party, bring it to power in the state and sit in this position. I continued to think about it even while I was in jail," he said. He thanked the people of Kanakapura for their continued support and said their love and blessings had played a major role in his political journey. Shivakumar said no one was permanent and that every person received an opportunity in life to leave behind meaningful contributions to society. He said he came from a middle-class family, grew up in a village and had engaged in poultry farming, agriculture and various businesses before entering politics."Criticism will die, but the work we do will remain," he said. Stressing the importance of humanity, Shivakumar said people should not be divided on the basis of caste or colour."Our sweat is salty, and everyone's blood is red. Humanity is what matters," he said. He also urged youngsters to believe in hard work rather than luck, saying success required discipline, concentration, difficult decisions and sacrifice. Referring to technological changes, Shivakumar said the younger generation was growing up with technologies such as artificial intelligence, Google and ChatGPT, and society must adapt to ensure that knowledge and experience reach people in every possible form. He said Mysuru had a rich historical legacy and should grow alongside Bengaluru, adding that economic activity and employment opportunities should be expanded across other cities rather than being concentrated in one place.--IANSmka/dan

title: Cabinet approves Rs 5,000 crore for continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
excerpt: New Delhi, November 11 (IANS): The government on Wednesday approved the continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) with a corpus of Rs 5,000 crore for a period of five years, up to December 31, 2031. The scheme will act as a catalyst to young aspiring entrepreneurs to set up and grow their business. The extension of the scheme will enable loans of Rs 12.6 lakh crore over the next five years. The scheme provides credit guarantee coverage to the lending institutions through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) against default risk, according to the Union Cabinet. As on September 2026, more than 60.36 crore loans amounting to Rs 43.34 lakh crore have been sanctioned by lending institutions since the launch of PM Mudra Scheme. The CGFMU, which was launched in January 2016, has acted as a major catalyst in enabling the growth of PMMY loans in the country. The purpose of the fund is to provide guarantee to lending institutions for loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) up to Rs 20 lakh; overdraft of up to Rs 10,000 provided by banks under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts; and loans granted to Self Help Group (SHG) where portfolio is between Rs.10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh. Also, the guaranteed coverage is linked to the disbursement amount in case of working capital limits and outstanding amount for term loan accounts to reflect the actual risk exposure of lending institutions. The scheme would be applicable to all loans extended under PMMY during the XVIth Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31).According to an official statement, collateral free loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) have created a whole new generation of entrepreneurs who previously could not avail loans from the formal banking system.

title: Maha CM banks on dedicated policy for nuclear power, reaffirms push for storage and data centres
excerpt: Mumbai, Nov 11 (IANS) Signalling a major strategic shift toward long-term energy security, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that the state is formulating a dedicated nuclear energy policy with a core focus on Small Modular Reactors (SMRs). Speaking to journalists during a Diwali media interaction at his official residence, Varsha, he underlined nuclear energy and pumped storage hydro projects as vital, non-negotiable pillars for supplying clean, baseload power to the state's expanding economy. Highlighting the physical constraints of conventional installations, CM Fadnavis emphasised the operational agility of Small Modular Reactors, nuclear power units designed to generate up to 300 MW. "The state will host both large-scale nuclear power projects and small modular reactors through private sector participation alongside state-owned ventures," he stated. Custom Ad: Multiplex "We are particularly focusing on SMRs due to their compact footprint and reduced land requirement. The Maharashtra government recently dispatched a delegation to the United States to study advanced SMR deployments," he added. The policy groundwork follows a landmark move on May 20, 2026, when the Maharashtra government signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) aiming to generate 25,400 MW of nuclear power through a projected investment of Rs 6.5 lakh crore. State generation utility Mahagenco is set to directly participate in nuclear generation alongside private enterprise partners. Addressing safety and environmental concerns, CM Fadnavis dismissed opposition to nuclear installations by citing the Tarapur Atomic Power Station in Palghar: "Tarapur has operated smoothly and safely for over four decades without incident." Commenting on the controversy regarding tree felling for a proposed pumped hydro storage project in Karjat taluka, Raigad district, CM Fadnavis mounted a strong defence of grid-scale energy storage along the Sahyadri mountain range. He explained that pumped storage operates on a closed-loop system, using off-peak solar power to pump water from lower reservoirs back to upper dams, allowing the same water volume to generate hydroelectricity repeatedly during peak hours. "Once these projects are operational, citizens will realise their structural benefits," CM Fadnavis noted, assuring that mandatory compensatory afforestation programs enforced on project developers will restore and support local forest ecosystems. In response to public debate over resource allocation for AI Data Centres in Thane and near Solapur’s Ujani Dam, CM Fadnavis framed digital infrastructure as a priority for national data sovereignty and economic competitiveness. To mitigate environmental impact, the state will mandate strict water and power efficiency benchmarks. "Data centres in the Thane and Navi Mumbai belts will be required to utilise treated wastewater or desalinated seawater rather than diverting local municipal drinking water. As high-yield commercial enterprises, data centres will absorb higher power tariffs, effectively cross-subsidising utility rates for domestic and agricultural power consumers," said the Chief Minister. "Opposition to data centres stems either from misconceptions or pure political posturing," remarked CM Fadnavis. He added, "These projects are essential to modern national infrastructure, and we will ensure they operate efficiently without burdening public resources." --IANS sj/dan

As high-yield commercial enterprises, data centres will absorb higher power tariffs, effectively cross-subsidising utility rates for domestic and agricultural power consumers," said the Chief Minister."Opposition to data centres stems either from misconceptions or pure political posturing," remarked CM Fadnavis. He added, "These projects are essential to modern national infrastructure, and we will ensure they operate efficiently without burdening public resources."

title: Gokul Milk Union Election 2026: CM Devendra Fadnavis Defends Nominated Directors As Mahayuti's Rajesh Patil Wins Chairman's Post
excerpt: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis defended appointing four directors to Kolhapur's Gokul cooperative, citing a legal deadlock in its chairman's election. He said rival factions held 13 and 12 elected seats, preventing the required quorum. The Bombay High Court directed that nominees' votes be counted separately. Mahayuti-backed Rajesh Patil subsequently won the chairman's post by 16 votes to 13.

title: Madras High Court Seeks Publisher-Wise Audit Of Tamil Nadu Public Library Book Purchases, Flags Possible Digital Manipulation
excerpt: The Madras High Court sought detailed records of Tamil Nadu public library book purchases amid allegations of procurement irregularities and possible digital manipulation. The court demanded publisher-wise purchase and payment details, while suggesting disclosure of two decades of procurement data. Vigilance authorities have launched an inquiry and frozen three bank accounts containing ₹22 lakh.

title: Maharashtra Drought 2026: 'No Immediate Plans To Run Jaldoot Water Trains Despite 305 Talukas Affected,' Says CM Devendra Fadnavis
excerpt: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis said special water trains are not needed immediately despite drought affecting 305 of the state's 358 talukas. Responding to The Free Press Journal, he said the government would deploy trains if required. Over eight lakh farmers have been affected. In 2016, the Jaldoot service made 111 trips to supply water to drought-hit Latur.
